# GitHub Copilot Instructions for `sahil_portfolio`

This is a **bare‑bones Flutter portfolio application** generated by `flutter create`.
Almost all of the logic lives in `lib/main.dart`, and the rest of the repository
is the platform scaffolding produced by the Flutter tool (Android, iOS, macOS,
Linux, Windows, and web).  When working as an AI assistant, you can treat this
project as a normal Flutter workspace with the following specifics:

## 📁 Project structure

- `lib/main.dart` – single entry point.  Currently renders a `MaterialApp` with
  a `Text('Hello World!')`.  New features will generally involve adding new
  Dart files under `lib/` and updating this file.
- `pubspec.yaml` – dependencies, assets, and other Flutter configuration.  Run
  `flutter pub get` whenever you edit it.
- `android/`, `ios/`, `macos/`, `linux/`, `windows/`, `web/` – platform-specific
  code generated by Flutter; modifying them is rarely necessary unless you
  introduce a new plugin or need to tweak native settings.
- `assets/` – static files referenced from Dart code.  Add assets here and
  declare them in `pubspec.yaml`.

## 🚧 Build & run workflows

The standard Flutter commands apply:

```bash
# fetch packages
flutter pub get

# run on iOS simulator
flutter run -d ios

# run on Android emulator
flutter run -d android

# build for release
flutter build apk          # Android
flutter build ios          # iOS
flutter build web          # Web
flutter build macos/linux/windows  # Desktop platforms
```

Open the root directory in Android Studio, IntelliJ, or VS Code and use the
Flutter plugins for debugging.  No custom Gradle tasks or scripts are added.

## 🧱 Architectural notes

- The portfolio now consists of a set of independent "section" widgets
  under `lib/sections/` such as `HeaderSection`, `AboutSection`,
  `SkillsSection`, etc.  Each contains static content drawn from
  `assets/Sahil_Resume_Nov_2025.pdf`.  Maintain this pattern when adding new
  sections or updating layout.
- Follow Flutter conventions: widgets are immutable, favor composition over
  inheritance, and use `setState`, `Provider`, `Riverpod`, etc. only if the
  app evolves to multi-screen complexity.
- Platform integration uses the normal `pubspec` plugins.  For example, to
  access device features add the plugin to `pubspec.yaml` and run `flutter pub
  get`.

## 🔧 Project-specific conventions

- Code formatting is handled by `dartfmt`/`flutter format` – always run it or
  rely on the editor's format-on-save.
- Tests aren’t currently present; follow Flutter's `test/` directory layout if
  they are added later.
- There are no custom lint rules beyond the default generated by `analysis_options.yaml`.

## 📎 Integration points & dependencies

- External dependencies live in `pubspec.yaml`.  The project already uses
  `url_launcher` for opening mailto links, external URLs, and the resume PDF.
- Assets are declared in `pubspec.yaml` and currently include the resume PDF
  under `assets/Sahil_Resume_Nov_2025.pdf`.  Web builds serve this file at the
  same relative path so `launchUrl(Uri.parse('assets/Sahil_Resume_Nov_2025.pdf'))`
  opens it.
- Native platform code is untouched.  If you add a plugin, Flutter will modify
  the corresponding platform directories automatically.
- The project does not communicate with any external web services at the
  moment; network code would be added in Dart under `lib/` if needed.

## 📝 Guidance for AI agents

When you or another AI agent generates code:

1. **Keep changes within `lib/` unless a platform change is truly required.**
   Most features can be implemented purely in Dart.
2. **Mention the build commands** above if you modify `pubspec.yaml` or add
   assets, since human developers will need to run `flutter pub get`.
3. **Refer back to this file** for future instructions – it should stay
   concise and reflect the current state of the repository.
4. Avoid adding boilerplate for systems (state management, network layers,
   etc.) until there’s evidence in the repo that they’re used.
5. Test additions by running `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` if tests are
   present; call out any analyzer warnings.

> _Note:_ Because the codebase is so small, there is no need to document
> service boundaries or complex data flows yet.  Focus on preserving the simple
> MaterialApp structure and on making sure any new files are imported correctly.
